Q3752768.summary: The Virgin sits frontally on a throne, crowned and wrapped in a red mantle over a blue robe, holding the Christ Child before her with both hands as he sits upright on her lap. Today the statue is enshrined beneath a silver crown held by two angels within a silver wreath. As a 'Seat of Wisdom', she offers the Child to the pilgrims who climb to this high Pyrenean valley.
facts: Although tradition says Saint Giles carved the image while living as a hermit at Núria around 700–703, the statue now venerated is a Romanesque carving of polychromed walnut usually dated to the 12th century.
According to legend the image was found in 1079, together with Saint Giles's cross, bell and cooking pot; the custom of putting one's head into the pot and ringing the bell survives at the shrine.
The Virgin of Núria received a canonical coronation in 1965 and is principal patron of the diocese of Urgell.

links.label: Viquipèdia (Catalan): Mare de Déu de Núria

Q3752768.notes: Wikidata's '9th century' reflects the legend rather than the object; Catalan Wikipedia gives 12th (or 12th–13th) century. This moves the work out of the 8th–11th-century batch.

cur:catacombs-liebieghaus-sarcophagus.summary: At the left a praying woman appears in a round medallion; beside it Christ, among bearded apostles holding loaves, multiplies the bread, with baskets at the base. The deeply undercut heads and drapery give the relief a vivid immediacy.
facts: The museum dates it to about 330 (inv. 1501).

Q116244842.summary: This small hexagonal censer of silver, partly gilded, hangs from three chains. Under an arcade of twisted columns on each of its six faces stands a gilded holy figure: Christ holding a Gospel book, the Virgin with hands raised in prayer, Saints Peter (with a cross) and Paul, and two winged angels. As incense rose from it during the liturgy, the vessel surrounded worshippers with an image of the heavenly court gathered around Christ.
facts: The Met dates the censer to ca. 582–602, the span of the reign of Emperor Maurice.
Greek inscriptions run along the upper rim above the arcades.
It is small: 8.9 cm high and 13.2 cm across, weighing about 364 g.
Q116244842.notes: Acc. 1985.123. The Met's object page text was not accessible (bot-blocked), so identifications rest on the Met's subject tags (Christ, Virgin, Peter, Paul) and on the photographs; the two winged figures are clearly angels but are not named here. The reason for the precise date range was not confirmed.
